prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour’s 2015 manifesto is a plan for national renewal built on a simple truth: Britain only succeeds when working people succeed. It couples fiscal responsibility with social justice, devolves power, and ensures everyone—especially those at the top—plays by the same rules.

Budget Responsibility Lock: Every pledge is fully funded with no extra borrowing. Labour will cut the deficit every year, get debt falling, aim for a current budget surplus as soon as possible, and legislate for independent OBR audits of all major parties’ manifestos.

Fair, productive economy: Labour will create a high-skill, high-wage economy—raising the National Minimum Wage to over £8 by 2019; banning exploitative zero-hours contracts; promoting the Living Wage via procurement and first-year tax rebates; and scrapping employment tribunal fees. Taxes will be fair: a new 10p starting rate; no rise in basic or higher Income Tax, NI or VAT; reversal of the 50p tax cut for incomes over £150,000; abolition of non-dom status; and a clampdown on avoidance and loopholes. To boost productivity, Labour will back small firms (cut and then freeze business rates), create a British Investment Bank and regional banks, strengthen challenger banks, and levy payday lenders. Long-termism will be hard-wired through corporate governance reform, employee voice on pay, and a National Infrastructure Commission to drive HS2, northern rail, roads, cycling, universal high-speed broadband, and a million green jobs with a 2030 clean power target and stronger Green Investment Bank.

Mending broken markets and the cost of living: Freeze energy bills to 2017 and reform the market; drive home energy efficiency; introduce a national water affordability scheme; reform rail with a public operator option, fare freeze and caps; empower city/county regions over buses and integrated ticketing.

World-class public services: Rescue and integrate the NHS—20,000 more nurses, 8,000 more GPs, 3,000 more midwives funded by a Mansion Tax on £2m+ properties, a tobacco levy and anti-avoidance; 48‑hour GP access; one‑week cancer tests; parity for mental health; prevention on obesity and alcohol; repeal the Health and Social Care Act and cap private profits. Social care will end 15‑minute visits, recruit 5,000 home‑care workers, and support carers. Education funding protected from early years to post‑16; all teachers qualified; smaller classes for 5–7‑year‑olds; local Directors of School Standards; a gold‑standard technical route (Technical Baccalaureate, Institutes of Technical Education).

Families, housing, social security: Extend free childcare to 25 hours for working parents of 3–4‑year‑olds; guarantee wraparound care 8am–6pm; double paternity leave and pay. Build at least 200,000 homes a year by 2020; three‑year private tenancies with limits on excessive rent rises; ban letting fees; crack down on land banking; abolish the Bedroom Tax. Keep the benefit cap, restore contribution, tailor back‑to‑work support, reform disability assessments with dignity, and maintain the pensions triple lock.

Immigration, safety, extremism: Control with fair rules—1,000 extra border staff, full exit checks, two‑year wait for EU migrants’ benefits, English requirement for public‑facing roles, and a new law to stop wage undercutting. Protect neighbourhood policing by safeguarding over 10,000 officers, abolish PCCs, create a Victims’ Law, and legislate against violence towards women and girls. Confront extremism with stronger, proportionate powers, mandatory de‑radicalisation for Syria returnees, and tougher oversight—while upholding rights.

Power to people: End a century of centralisation with an English Devolution Act transferring £30bn and powers over transport, skills, housing and business support; a people‑led Constitutional Convention; replace the House of Lords with a Senate of the Nations and Regions; votes at 16; a tougher lobbyist register; ban MPs’ paid directorships; gender pay gap reporting; implement Leveson; expand FOI and open data.

Britain in the world: Remain in and reform the EU with a referendum lock on any transfer of powers; strengthen NATO ties; conduct an SDSR; maintain a minimum, credible independent nuclear deterrent; lead on human rights (LGBT and Religious Freedom envoys); meet the 0.7% aid commitment; and push for a Paris deal consistent with net zero global emissions in the second half of the century.

Fully funded, fair, and outward‑looking, this programme makes Britain work for working people—and asks everyone to do their part.
